t: This is St George's, Bloomsbury, a parish church designed by Nicholas Hawksmoor and consecrated in 1730. Hawksmoor was a leading figure of English Baroque who worked alongside Christopher Wren and John Vanbrugh, and he contributed to St Paul's Cathedral, Greenwich Hospital, Blenheim Palace and Castle Howard. The church is named for Saint George, the early Christian martyr who is especially venerated as a military saint. Down in the crypt you will find the Museum of Comedy. The barrister Samuel Courthope Bosanquet was also born here.
